previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with altered mental status and weakness following a fall, in the context of relapsed multiple myeloma. His confusion was attributed to hypercalcemia (calcium 10.7), which improved with IV fluids and pamidronate. He had an elevated creatinine of 1.7, consistent with acute kidney injury likely due to dehydration and hypercalcemia, which resolved with treatment. A single blood culture grew coagulase-negative staph, but it was deemed a contaminant given no fever and negative repeat cultures; IV vancomycin was discontinued. His multiple myeloma remained active, and he missed a scheduled daratumumab dose, which was rescheduled post-discharge. He was managed for diabetes with insulin, continued lamivudine for hepatitis B, and treated for constipation with stool softeners. His mental status normalized, and he was discharged home with services in stable condition.

congestion. There is also concern about progression of his

dexamethasone 40mg.

He has reported ""gasping"" for breath recently with exertion, 
which he attributes to fatigue. Denies orthopnea or PND. He has 
occasionally had to lower himself to the ground at home because 
he was too weak to continue walking. Denies head strike.

Currently, he reports feeling well with no complaints, other 
than his ongoing back pain. He feels that his thinking is clear 
and has not noticed any changes recently. As I was leaving the

Brief Hospital Course:
___ with relapsed refractory multiple myeloma, h/o bilateral 
PEs, HTN, T2DM who presents with confusion, hypercalcemia, now 
with course c/b hyperglycemia and hypertension.

# Relapsed refractory myeloma: On admission patient was treated 
with 4 day pulse of dexamethasone. Because of failure of 
outpatient daratumumab, he was further started on 
dexamethasone/velcade/Cytoxan in ___ with close monitoring of 
blood sugars and blood pressures. He will continue to follow up 
with outpatient provider ___. 

# Hyperglycemia | Type 2 diabetes: In setting of receiving 
dexamethasone patient had very elevated blood sugars in house 
with BGs. He was seen by ___ consult service and briefly 
required insulin drip as well as insulin doses significantly 
increased from baseline. He will follow up with his outpatient 
endocrinologist.

# Hypertension: Patient with poorly controlled hypertension as 
outpatient. Pressures were even more elevated here in setting of 
dexamethasone. His home diltiazem was increased, carvedilol was 
continued, and amlodipine 5 mg was added. HE should follow up 
with his PCP and outpatient cardiologist.

# Hypercalcemia: Calcium was 11.3 in clinic, likely due to 
ongoing multiple myeloma. He was given 60 mg pamidronate in 
clinic with resolution of hypercalcemia.

# Acute kidney injury on chronic kidney disease: Cr 1.7 on 
admission, from baseline around 1.1-1.2. Thought likely from 
hypercalcemia, hyperglycemia/dehydration, myeloma progression, 
poorly controlled DM2. Improved to 1.3 on day of discharge.

# Altered mental status: Unclear etiology; may have been in 
setting of mild hypercalcemia. Resolved by time of admission.

# Dyspnea: Patient reported dyspnea on admission. CXR 
unremarkable, and VQ scan was normal. Given concern for 
symptomatic anemia he was transfused with 1U pRBCs. Symptoms 
were improved at time of discharge.

# History of C. difficle infection: Continued PO vancomycin 125 
mg daily.
